posts.cooked:
Where does the bug appear (feature/product)?

Grok Bot

Describe the Bug

Product: Grok Bot / Gmail MCP
Account: aviv@theaviv.ca
Namespace: user-Gmail–professional-aviv-theaviv-ca

Grok Bot’s Gmail connector cannot search Spam even though the label metadata reports Spam threads.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Call list_labels — SPAM showed threadsTotal=3, threadsUnread=3.
  2. Call search_threads with query in:spam.
  3. Also try label:SPAM, is:spam, and broader queries with includeTrash.
  4. Compare with an Inbox search.

Expected Behavior

search_threads returns the Spam threads so an agent can review Spam without using the browser.

Operating System

Other

Version Information

N/A — Gmail MCP connector issue; no Grok Bot version information available.

Additional Information

Actual: search_threads returns empty {} every time. Inbox search works, while list_labels still shows the Spam count.

Impact: cannot review or empty Spam via the connector for a query form the tool docs claim (in:spam / label:SPAM). Forced browser fallback.

Also filed via in-app Send Feedback and by email to hi@cursor.com from aviv@theaviv.ca (thread subject: Grok Bot Gmail: search_threads returns empty for Spam while list_labels shows 3 threads).

Does this stop you from using Cursor

No - Cursor works, but with this issue

posts.name: Dean Rie
posts.cooked:
Hey, thanks for the detailed report.

The Gmail connector works on top of Google’s hosted Gmail server, and its search excludes Spam and Trash by default. The includeTrash option only adds Trash, and in:spam / label:SPAM / is:spam don’t override that default. That’s why you get an empty result even though list_labels still shows a count.

The documented way to reach Spam is the in:anywhere operator. Can you try it and tell me what you get back?

  1. Ask the bot to call search_threads with this exact request: in:anywhere label:SPAM
  2. If it’s empty, try search_threads with: in:anywhere is:unread your 3 Spam threads are unread, so they should show up with the SPAM label id
  3. Reply here with whether step 1 or step 2 returned threads, or if it’s still empty.

One expectation note: the connector can move threads to Trash or Spam and change labels, but Google’s server doesn’t expose a permanent delete tool. So you can’t “clear” Spam through the connector right now, even once the threads are found.

Let me know what in:anywhere shows, since the next steps depend on that.

posts.name: Dean Rie
posts.cooked:
Thanks for testing both options and catching the nuance. You got it right.

Since list_labels currently shows SPAM with threadsTotal=0 / threadsUnread=0, an empty response for a Spam request is expected and doesn’t really confirm the original issue. The fact that in:anywhere is:unread returned threads also confirms the connector itself is working fine.

To fully close this out, we need one conclusive run exactly when there are emails in Spam again. At that moment, please call search_threads with this exact request:

in:anywhere label:SPAM

This operator is documented on the hosted Gmail server as the way to reach Spam and Trash, unlike in:spam / label:SPAM / is:spam / includeTrash, which don’t override the default behavior. Please reply here with whether it returns those threads or still returns {}. The next steps depend on that.

On permanent delete, yep, that’s correct. The connector can move items to Trash or Spam and change labels, but Google doesn’t expose a tool for permanent deletion, so we can’t clear Spam through the connector right now.

posts.name: Aviv Yeshayav
posts.cooked:
Retest just now on aviv@theaviv.ca (2026-09-08 ~4pm America/Toronto). Spam has mail again.

list_labels SPAM: threadsTotal=1, threadsUnread=1, messagesTotal=1.

  1. search_threads query in:anywhere label:SPAM → empty {}.
    1. search_threads query in:anywhere in:spam → empty {}.
    1. search_threads with includeTrash=true and query in:anywhere label:SPAM → empty {}.
    1. search_threads query in:anywhere is:unread → returns normal unread inbox threads (works). The Spam thread is not among them.
      So with Spam non-empty, Dean’s documented in:anywhere path still cannot list Spam. Same mismatch as the original report (email T-F54576). Browser Gmail still shows the Spam thread.

posts.name: Dean Rie
posts.cooked:
Thanks for seeing it through and running the final test with a non-empty Spam folder. That was the conclusive run we were missing.

The outcome is clear. With list_labels, SPAM shows threadsTotal=1, but the documented request in:anywhere label:SPAM and all other Spam variants still return {}. At the same time, in:anywhere is:unread works and the thread is visible in the Gmail browser UI. So this isn’t about your setup or the connector itself. The behavior is on the hosted Gmail server side that the connector talks to directly. We pass arguments as-is, without rewriting the request or filtering the results.

I’ve shared this with the team along with your steps, so we can raise it upstream. I can’t share a timeline yet, but I’ll post here if there’s an update.

On permanent delete, it’s as discussed. The connector can move threads to Trash or Spam and change labels, but Google doesn’t expose an API for final deletion. So we can’t “clear” Spam through the connector right now. Until Spam search works, using the browser fallback is still a workable workaround for reviewing Spam.

posts.name: Talos Dreams
posts.cooked:
I am also requesting same gmail spam access from grok bot for spam header analysis and spam filter updates.

(Lest anyone things Aviv is alone in this.)

My Grok Bot would like to clarify the following:

= = = =

Dean — the default hide of SPAM/TRASH is Google’s. The gap is still on this connector.

Google’s users.threads.list / users.messages.list already document two opt-ins that return Spam:

• includeSpamTrash=true

• labelIds=SPAM

Google for Developers

Method: users.threads.list  |  Gmail  |  Google for Developers

This tool only exposes includeTrash plus q=. That is why in:spam, label:SPAM, is:spam, and in:anywhere label:SPAM all return {} while list_labels still shows a Spam count.

in:anywhere is a Gmail search-box operator. It is not a substitute for those two list parameters. On the API, q= still omits Spam unless one of those flags is set.

So: not a bad login, not an empty folder. Google’s hosted API can list Spam. This MCP wrapper never sends the parameter that asks for it. Please expose includeSpamTrash and/or labelIds (including SPAM) on search_threads / list.

= = = =

Talos

posts.name: Dean Rie
posts.cooked:
Hey Talos, thanks for the detailed write-up and for confirming you’re not the only one running into this.

You nailed the technical detail. in:anywhere is a search string operator, and it’s not equivalent to the list parameters includeSpamTrash=true or labelIds=SPAM that Google documents for users.threads.list and users.messages.list. I shared this exact observation with the team. The connector currently only passes through includeTrash plus q= and doesn’t set those two parameters for search_threads. This is a useful angle, separate from what we discussed with Aviv above.

The issue is already being tracked. I can’t share an ETA yet, but I’ll reply in the thread if there’s an update. For now, since server-side Spam search isn’t available through the connector, the browser fallback is still the working option to view Spam.

If you notice any change in behavior on your side, let me know and I’ll add it to what we have.
